allObjections.title: Construction engine 0% success rate
allObjections.detail: Section B shows 26 construction-class envelopes on reltwin with 0 construction_complete - the engine has never successfully completed a single run. Building FlowAI MVP on a foundation that has 100% failure rate violates CA-18 §1's quality guarantee of substantial transformation per run.

allObjections.title: Self-application produces empty payloads
allObjections.detail: Section A shows 4 self-runs all with empty payload, directly violating CA-18 §5's requirement that FlowAI applies to its own development process. The system cannot improve itself if self-runs produce no actionable output.

allObjections.title: Missing 85% of quality dimensions
allObjections.detail: Section A shows §2 Quality Dims at ~15% with 6/10 dimensions silently omitted and no jurisdiction column. CA-18 §1 requires perfection across ALL quality dimensions - shipping with 15% coverage violates the core promise.

allObjections.title: Tool Intelligence has zero call sites
allObjections.detail: Section A shows §6 Tool Intelligence at ~35% with 0 call sites and 0 tool.selection envelopes despite ToolIntelligenceService being built. A service with no integration points cannot deliver intelligent tool selection as required.

allObjections.title: Lack of rollback mechanism
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not specify a rollback mechanism for changes made by FlowAI, particularly in the event of a failure or error during the construction process. This could lead to incomplete or incorrect deployments without a clear path to revert to a previous stable state.

allObjections.title: Incomplete self-application process
allObjections.detail: In §5, the proposal mentions FlowAI's self-application capabilities but notes that the flowai.construction_eligible flag is set to FALSE and self-runs produce empty payloads. This indicates that the self-improvement cycle is not fully operational, which could undermine the tool's ability to refine itself effectively.

allObjections.title: Potential for user confusion
allObjections.detail: The user agency section in §1 emphasizes user control over iteration depth, but the complexity of the information provided (e.g., score trajectories, diminishing returns) may overwhelm users, leading to suboptimal decision-making or disengagement from the process.

allObjections.title: Lack of Rollback
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide a clear rollback strategy in case of failures or errors during the construction process, which could lead to data loss or corruption. Specifically, §1 Core Definition does not mention any rollback mechanisms.

allObjections.title: Insufficient Error Handling
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide sufficient details on error handling and debugging mechanisms, which could lead to difficulties in identifying and resolving issues. For example, §3 Iteration does not specify how errors are handled during the iteration process.

allObjections.title: Unclear Construction Engine
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide a clear explanation of the construction engine and its components, which could lead to difficulties in understanding and implementing the system. Specifically, §5 Symbiotic Meta-Principle mentions the construction engine, but does not provide sufficient details.

allObjections.title: Incomplete §2 Quality Dimensions
allObjections.detail: The proposal notes that §2 Quality Dimensions are only ~15% complete with 6/10 dimensions silently omitted and no jurisdiction column. This incomplete implementation could lead to unreliable quality assessments and poor user experiences.

allObjections.title: Unreliable Construction Engine
allObjections.detail: The construction engine has 26 construction-class envelopes on reltwin with 0 construction_complete, indicating significant issues with end-to-end construction. This could lead to failed builds and unreliable outputs.

allObjections.title: Lack of Honest Assessment Gate
allObjections.detail: The pre-run honest-gate is only ~15% complete, which means FlowAI may not accurately communicate when a product already meets quality standards. This could result in unnecessary iterations and wasted resources.

allObjections.title: Incomplete Quality Dimensions
allObjections.detail: The proposal fails to address the incomplete implementation of §2 quality dimensions, which are critical for evaluating the output of FlowAI.

allObjections.title: Unresolved Construction Aborts
allObjections.detail: The 26 construction_attempt_aborted envelopes on reltwin indicate unresolved issues in the construction engine that need to be debugged and fixed.

allObjections.title: Lack of Tool Intelligence Integration
allObjections.detail: The Tool Intelligence service is built but has no call sites, indicating a lack of integration which is essential for the proposed FlowAI MVP.

allObjections.title: Oversimplified MVP scope
allObjections.detail: Dropping jurisdiction/access/privacy/legal from §2 in the MVP scope (D) introduces significant risk. These dimensions are crucial for real-world applicability and ignoring them early could lead to architectural issues later. This simplification might create a false sense of progress.

allObjections.title: Unclear 'substantial transformation'
allObjections.detail: §1's 'substantial transformation' quality guarantee lacks a clear, measurable definition. This ambiguity makes it difficult to objectively assess whether a run is a success or failure, potentially leading to subjective interpretations and inconsistent results. The lack of a quantitative threshold undermines the guarantee's value.

allObjections.title: Self-application risks
allObjections.detail: §5's self-application of FlowAI to its own development process could lead to a feedback loop of increasingly complex and potentially unstable code. Without careful monitoring and control, this self-improvement cycle could introduce unintended consequences and make the system harder to understand and maintain.

allObjections.title: Honest assessment subjectivity
allObjections.detail: §1's 'honest assessment' relies on FlowAI proactively communicating when a product already meets the quality standard. This assessment is inherently subjective and could be influenced by biases or incomplete information, leading to inaccurate recommendations and potentially hindering genuine improvements.

allObjections.title: §2 Quality Dims incomplete
allObjections.detail: Current implementation only covers 6/10 quality dimensions with no jurisdiction handling, violating CA-18 §1's quality guarantee. This risks producing outputs that appear compliant but fail key metrics like accessibility or legal alignment.

allObjections.title: Construction engine non-functional
allObjections.detail: 26 construction attempts aborted with 0 completions (A.8) indicates core S1-S8 gates are failing in production. MVP can't deliver URL-in/URL-out without fixing this first-order failure in src/lib/construction/.

allObjections.title: Self-application gap
allObjections.detail: flowai.construction_eligible=FALSE (A.5) blocks CA-18 §5's symbiotic principle. Four empty self-runs show FlowAI can't yet improve itself - critical path for long-term viability remains unproven.

allObjections.title: UI-first assumes working engine
allObjections.detail: The K1 UI-FIRST path wires `/api/run-construction` and LandingPage submission before proving the underlying construction engine can actually complete end-to-end. The proposal itself states there are 26 `construction_attempt_aborted` envelopes and 0 `construction_complete` envelopes, so this sequencing risks building a polished shell around an unresolved failure mode.

allObjections.title: Demo path can diverge silently
allObjections.detail: The K1 DEMO-RELIABLE-PATH-FIRST option explicitly hard-codes a reliable demo and then generalizes backwards. That creates a high risk of a bifurcated system where the shown path succeeds while the general path remains audit-only or brittle, which undermines the stated goal of a real operator-reachable URL-in/URL-out product.

allObjections.title: Week-one deliverable is under-specified
allObjections.detail: K3 options talk about emitting `construction_complete.v1`, flipping `construction_eligible`, or replacing `/api/run.js`, but none gives a crisp acceptance criterion for correctness beyond internal envelopes or a single curl. There is no explicit rollback, no negative test, and no guarantee that the verified artifact corresponds to a durable user-visible capability rather than a one-off debug event.

allObjections.title: Lack of rollback path
allObjections.detail: The proposal under §D (Pre-decided scope) does not mention a rollback path for changes made by FlowAI, which could lead to irreversible damage if the construction engine or Tool Intelligence service malfunctions.

allObjections.title: Insufficient testing
allObjections.detail: The proposal mentions E2E Playwright (~20h) but does not specify how comprehensive the testing will be, potentially leaving critical edge cases untested.

allObjections.title: Risk of demo path divergence
allObjections.detail: The DEMO-RELIABLE-PATH-FIRST option under K1 risks creating a demo path that diverges from the general path, potentially leading to maintenance issues or inconsistencies.

allObjections.title: §2 Quality Dims FAIL unaddressed
allObjections.detail: Verified facts table lists §2 Quality Dims at FAIL (~15%) with 6/10 dimensions silently omitted and no jurisdiction column, yet no K1 option sequences dimension envelope restoration before exposing UI submit at LandingPage.jsx:442.

allObjections.title: 26 aborts ignored in UI-FIRST
allObjections.detail: Proposal states 26 construction-class envelopes on reltwin with 0 construction_complete and engine starts but never finishes, but UI-FIRST begins /api/run-construction wiring without first resolving any S8 Phase B abort via ConstructionEngine.js.

allObjections.title: §5 self-application bypassed

objections.detail: The K1 DEMO-RELIABLE-PATH-FIRST option explicitly hard-codes a reliable demo and then generalizes backwards. That creates a high risk of a bifurcated system where the shown path succeeds while the general path remains audit-only or brittle, which undermines the stated goal of a real operator-reachable URL-in/URL-out product.

objections.title: Week-one deliverable is under-specified
objections.detail: K3 options talk about emitting `construction_complete.v1`, flipping `construction_eligible`, or replacing `/api/run.js`, but none gives a crisp acceptance criterion for correctness beyond internal envelopes or a single curl. There is no explicit rollback, no negative test, and no guarantee that the verified artifact corresponds to a durable user-visible capability rather than a one-off debug event.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If the team picks UI-FIRST or the demo-reliable path and the route returns a preview or stubbed success while the engine still aborts, users will see apparent progress without real construction. That is worse than the current honest audit-only state because it can mislead stakeholders into believing FlowAI is operational when it is not.
adversarial.precedent: The Therac-25 failures are a real-world precedent: a user-facing interface and workflow suggested operation while hidden internal state and insufficient validation produced catastrophic mismatch between perceived and actual behavior.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The strongest case for rejecting or deferring this proposal is that it optimizes for visible milestones before the core construction loop is verified. Because the artifact already shows empty self-runs, missing dimensions, and zero end-to-end construction completes, any roadmap that front-loads UI or demo reliability risks institutionalizing a partial system as if it were production-ready. A short deferral to stabilize the engine and define stricter verification would likely reduce rework and prevent confidence from outrunning capability.

K1.pick_text: CONSTRUCTION-LOOP-FIRST: W1-3 construction engine end-to-end against ANY product CLI (debug all aborts; first successful construction_complete). W4-5 UI submit triggers construction. W6-7 FlowAI-on-FlowAI cycle (canonical proof per CA-18 §5). W8-9 honest-gate + Tool Intelligence + dimensions envelope. W10-12 auth + observability + Sentry + polish + demo. Strongest CA-18 §5 alignment; slowest to UI-visible milestone.
K1.rationale: This is the least likely to create a deceptive demo because it forces a real construction-complete proof before UI polish. It also aligns best with the canonical self-application requirement in §5, even if it delays visible progress.

K2.pick_text: 13-16 weeks. Realistic with friction. Anticipates: (a) the empty-payload self-run debug takes longer than 15h budgeted; (b) auth + Sentry + rate-limit integration has hidden complexity; (c) E2E Playwright on real Vercel deploys requires retry-and-flake-handling work; (d) Victor's 10-15 hrs/wk has weeks where it dips below. Closer to upper-bound prior hours estimate.
K2.rationale: Given the documented aborts, empty payloads, and missing call sites, the lower buckets are too optimistic. This range better absorbs engine debug, integration friction, and verification overhead without pretending the remaining work is mostly wiring.

K3.pick_text: Debug empty-payload self-runs first. Time: 4-6 hrs. Files: src/lib/agents/renewal/orchestrator.js + scripts/run-orchestration.mjs (add debug logging). Action: run scripts/run-orchestration.mjs --product flowai with VERBOSE=1; trace where the orchestration_complete payload becomes empty before write. Fix the write path or the envelope construction. Verification (Victor EOD Day 1): 5th flowai self-run produces a governance_record entry with non-null mode/gtmReady/exitReason/finalScore/previewUrl fields. Foundational debug; unblocks §5.
K3.rationale: This is the best Day 1 choice because it attacks the specific failure already observed on FlowAI self-runs, instead of adding a new route atop broken output. It produces the most diagnostic value per hour and directly unblocks the self-application loop.

perReviewer.overallNotes: I am not endorsing the roadmap as written; the votes above reflect the least risky options among the listed choices. The proposal still needs stricter acceptance tests tied to durable end-to-end behavior, not just envelopes or UI affordances.

objections.title: Lack of rollback path
objections.detail: The proposal under §D (Pre-decided scope) does not mention a rollback path for changes made by FlowAI, which could lead to irreversible damage if the construction engine or Tool Intelligence service malfunctions.

objections.title: Insufficient testing
objections.detail: The proposal mentions E2E Playwright (~20h) but does not specify how comprehensive the testing will be, potentially leaving critical edge cases untested.

objections.title: Risk of demo path divergence
objections.detail: The DEMO-RELIABLE-PATH-FIRST option under K1 risks creating a demo path that diverges from the general path, potentially leading to maintenance issues or inconsistencies.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If the construction engine fails to produce a construction_complete.v1 envelope and the debug process is prolonged, the project could stall, making the system worse than the status quo by delaying progress without delivering tangible results.
adversarial.precedent: The Theranos case is a real-world precedent where a rushed development process without adequate testing and validation led to significant failures.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The proposal's aggressive timeline and scope could lead to a rushed implementation that overlooks critical risks or edge cases, potentially resulting in a lower quality product or significant rework down the line.

Slowest but most likely.
